result.explanation: Outputs ch1-4 fell to 900 us and ch5/6 to 0 at t=90.755, while the roll setpoint froze at 0. A manual kill-switch event follows at 91.836. The recording does not show who commanded the drop.

evidence.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch1] at t=90.755 s: 1556 -> 900 us (step -656, 82x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: Motor outputs dropped together to minimum at 90.755 s. ch2-4 show the same step (lines 103, 105, 107).

evidence.quote: CHANGE actuator.output[ch5] at t=90.755 s: 1500 -> 0 us (step -1500, 1000x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: The ch5/ch6 outputs, which sat at 1500 all flight, went to 0 at the same instant as the motors.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=91.836 s controller.event[log] ERROR: [commander] Manual kill-switch engaged
evidence.shows: The kill-switch event is logged after the output drop at 90.755 s. In the sequence tool the actuators left baseline at 89.745 and 91.868 s.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT control.attitude_setpoint[roll] was varying, then held 0 from t=90.752 s to the end of the recording (7.082 s, 71 samples)
evidence.shows: The roll setpoint froze at 0 and the yaw-rate setpoint jumped at 90.752 s (line 118), just before the output step. The controller side changed with the outputs.

evidence.quote: ANOMALY a3 t=76.483 s: vehicle.attitude[yaw] followed control.attitude_setpoint[yaw] worse for good (typical |error| 0.147 -> 2.575)
evidence.shows: Yaw tracking degraded from 76.483 s. It coincides with a yaw setpoint manoeuvre, and compare shows the setpoint's spread jumping. Likely not a fault.

checked.check: Sequence of changes from 70 to 92 s, against the 30 s before
checked.result: Attitude and yaw channels left baseline first, from 70.079 to 78.403 s. Baro altitude moved at 88.583 s and the actuators from 89.745 to 91.868 s. The kill-switch event came at 91.836.

checked.check: Compare at 86.447 (the SHIFT onset for ch2/4/5/6)
checked.result: No series froze. Tracking ratios were 3.08 (roll) and 1.97 (pitch). The CHANGE lines put the actuator step at 90.755 s, so the SHIFT time is a median artefact.
The yaw setpoint's spread went from 0.007 to 3.595 and yaw tracking error rose 10.72x. Roll and pitch tracking improved (ratio 0.36 and 0.35). The motors did not change.

checked.check: Gaps and constant channels in the sheet
checked.result: Gaps starting at 18.447, 56.078 and 72.459 s hit all series at once, which fits log or scheduling dropouts. ch7 and ch8 are 0 for the whole recording. ch5 and ch6 are 1500 until the kill.
There are no lessons, and the BEV family does not apply (px4_vehicle). Charge accounting is indeterminate; protection and restart checks do not apply.

effects.quote: EVENT t=97.386 s controller.event[log] WARNING: [commander] Manual control lost
effects.why: Comes after the disarm at 96.855 s, so it follows the shutdown.

effects.quote: EVENT t=96.855 s controller.event[vehicle_status] arming_state ARMED -> DISARMED
effects.why: Disarm follows the kill and the outputs held at 900.

effects.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch1] was varying, then held 900 from t=91.868 s to the end of the recording (5.978 s, 60 samples)
effects.why: The outputs hold at minimum after the kill. This is the consequence of the shutdown, not its cause.

safety_findings.statement: Recorded SOC change is not explained by the measured charge; the check is indeterminate because the estimator method is unknown. It does not bear on the output drop; treat SOC as unreliable here.

unknowns: Who or what commanded the drop in outputs at 90.755 s.
Whether the vehicle was landing, already on the ground, or airborne at the kill.
Whether the yaw tracking degradation from 76.483 s was a real control fault or a commanded yaw manoeuvre.

data_requests.what: RC inputs and kill-switch state, land-detector state and arming flags from the full ULG
data_requests.window: Last 20 s of this flight, up to the disarm
data_requests.why_needed: Decides between an operator kill and an autonomous or fault-driven output cut.

hypotheses.claim: The pilot or RC link commanded the kill, and the outputs dropped as designed.
hypotheses.because: The kill-switch event follows the output drop and the controller setpoints changed at the same instant. Whether it was commanded is not in this data.
hypotheses.observed_at: commander event log and output channels

hypotheses.claim: A control or estimator fault, shown by the degraded yaw tracking, led to the cut.
hypotheses.because: Yaw tracking worsened from 76.483 s, but compare shows a setpoint manoeuvre and roll and pitch tracking improved.

hypotheses.claim: A hardware or output-driver fault pulled the outputs down.
hypotheses.because: All motor channels moved together and the ch5/ch6 outputs changed too. Nothing differs between channels, so a single-part fault is not shown.

hypotheses.claim: Periodic gaps in all series are logging dropouts, not a vehicle fault.
hypotheses.because: Three gaps hit every series at the same times (18.447, 56.078, 72.459 s). They are unrelated to the kill and limit how finely the sequence can be resolved.

events.what: Simultaneous sample gaps in all series, three times
events.why: Same times in every series; logging or scheduling dropouts.
Coincides with a yaw setpoint manoeuvre; not shown to be a fault.

events.what: Motor outputs to 900 us and ch5/6 to 0 at 90.755 s
events.why: Simultaneous drop with no recorded commanding event.

events.what: Roll setpoint frozen at 0 and yaw-rate setpoint jump at 90.752 s
events.why: Controller side changes at the same instant as the output drop.
Logged after the output drop; may be the same event.

result.lesson: No earlier cases in the workspace; none apply.
result.reuse_when: Applies only if a PX4 log shows motor outputs stepping to minimum together at about the same instant as a manual kill-switch event and a roll setpoint frozen at zero.

action.action: Analyse the saved ULG file offline for the commander and RC topics
action.why: Settles whether the output drop was commanded by an operator or came from an autonomous or fault-driven cut. This sheet has no RC channels or land-detector state.
how: Open the stored .ulg on a desktop and plot manual_control_setpoint and the kill switch field in the last 10 s before the output step
Plot vehicle_land_detected and actuator_armed for the same window
Compare the time of the switch input with the output step at 90.755 s

outcomes.label: Switch input flips at about 90.75 s
outcomes.means: Operator or RC-commanded kill; the drop in outputs is expected behaviour, not a vehicle fault.
outcomes.then: Close as operator action; review the yaw tracking separately.

outcomes.label: No switch input before 91.8 s
outcomes.means: Outputs dropped before any commanded kill, so look at commander, mixer or output-driver paths.
outcomes.then: Request the PX4 commander and mixer topics and the ESC status.

outcomes.label: Switch input present while airborne
outcomes.means: A kill during flight; the question moves to why the operator triggered it.
outcomes.then: Ask the operator what they saw before the kill.
